speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Could you please describe the specific nature of the feeding difficulties and when the abdominal distension typically occurs? I would also like to know if the infant has had any episodes of bilious vomiting or if his stools are pale and foul-smelling.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant pass stool regularly, or is there a history of delayed meconium passage at birth and constipation? I would also like to know if there is a family history of cystic fibrosis or if the baby has had any recurrent respiratory infections.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the infant pass gas or stool, and have you noticed any signs of rectal bleeding or mucus in the diaper? I would also like to know if the abdominal distension is symmetric or if there are visible peristaltic waves.

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Abdominal X-Ray
Has the infant had any rectal bleeding or mucus in the diaper, and did he pass meconium within the first 48 hours of life?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Contrast Enema
Given the X-ray findings of dilated bowel segments with an empty rectum, I need to confirm if there is a transition zone indicative of Hirschsprung disease.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: A transition zone in the distal colon, compatible with Hirschsprung disease

speaker: Doctor
text: The imaging findings of a transition zone in the distal colon are classic for Hirschsprung disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hirschsprung disease
